subsystems.name: Cold-atom source
subsystems.role: creates a cloud of atoms at microkelvin temperatures so their quantum motion is simple.

subsystems.name: Laser and optics bench
subsystems.role: cools the atoms, splits and recombines their quantum paths.
parts: Raman beam pair with a precisely set frequency difference

subsystems.name: Interferometer and detector
subsystems.role: converts gravitational acceleration into a measurable phase shift.

subsystems.name: Inertial reference and isolation
subsystems.role: removes the sensor's own motion from the gravity signal.

subsystems.name: Control electronics
subsystems.role: runs the timing-critical sequence and turns photodiode counts into numbers.

subsystems.name: Survey platform
subsystems.role: moves the instrument over the ground or holds it still for long measurements.

buildSteps.title: Trap and cool the atoms
buildSteps.detail: Rubidium vapour is loaded into a magneto-optical trap, then cooled further in optical molasses to a few microkelvin — a thousandth of a degree above absolute zero.

buildSteps.title: Launch or hold the cloud
buildSteps.detail: A moving optical lattice throws the atoms upward in a fountain, or the cloud is simply released and left to fall.

buildSteps.title: Stabilise the lasers
buildSteps.detail: Lasers are locked to atomic transitions and to a stable optical cavity so the Raman pulse frequency difference stays exact to the hertz.

buildSteps.title: Split, redirect and recombine
buildSteps.detail: Three laser pulses act as beam splitters and mirrors for the atoms: the cloud is divided into two momentum states, separated, then recombined, so the two paths interfere.

buildSteps.title: Read the interference
buildSteps.detail: Laser-induced fluorescence reveals how many atoms ended in each output state; the imbalance encodes the local gravitational acceleration.

buildSteps.title: Subtract platform motion
buildSteps.detail: A classical accelerometer and tiltmeter record how the instrument itself moved, and those signals are removed from the atomic phase.

buildSteps.title: Pair two clouds for a gradient
buildSteps.detail: Two clouds stacked a metre or so apart share the same laser beams, so vibration cancels: this yields the vertical gravity gradient instead of absolute gravity.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and map
buildSteps.detail: Readings are compared with a known reference site or a classical absolute gravimeter, then taken along survey lines; the data are inverted into a density model showing voids, tunnels or ore bodies.

prerequisites.tech: Laser cooling and trapping of atoms
prerequisites.why: developed in the 1980s and confirmed by the 1997 Nobel Prize in Physics; without microkelvin clouds there is no usable interferometer.
gravity was first measured with interfering atoms in 1991; it is the core measurement principle.

prerequisites.tech: Narrow-linewidth, rugged diode lasers and fibre optics
prerequisites.why: the Raman beam pair must keep a frequency difference stable to the hertz while being shaken on a truck or aircraft.
lab systems fill a room; field instruments must shrink this without losing atom numbers.

prerequisites.tech: Field-proven vibration compensation and gravity gradiometry
prerequisites.why: moving-platform surveys only work if platform acceleration, tilt and Coriolis effects are measured and cancelled to microgal level.

pathway.milestone: commercial atom-interferometric absolute gravimeters with sensitivities near 10⁻⁸ m/s² (about one microgal) per measurement
pathway.unlocks: absolute gravity without a falling corner cube, in observatories and geodesy networks.

pathway.milestone: truck-mounted and borehole gravity gradiometers proven in mineral exploration and void detection
pathway.unlocks: mapping tunnels, karst, cavities and ore bodies without drilling or excavation.

pathway.milestone: airborne, drone and ship-borne quantum gravity surveys
pathway.unlocks: fast coverage of large areas for groundwater, mineral and civil-engineering work.

pathway.milestone: satellite quantum gravimetry and shared cold-atom inertial navigation hardware
pathway.unlocks: global gravity mapping for ice and water mass, plus drift-free inertial navigation where satellite signals are unavailable.
